BreakdownRow.description: A labelled count in a horizontal bar list.
BreakdownRow.title: BreakdownRow

CourtSide.description: One half of the court: the side a point is played from, or where a ball lands.
CourtSide.title: CourtSide

CourtZoneCount.description:
How many of a style's final balls landed in one zone of the court.

Seven zones: the four in-court cells, deuce or ad by short or deep, and the
three ways a ball goes out, net, long and wide.
CourtZoneCount.title: CourtZoneCount

CurrentStreak.description: The latest result, and how many matches in a row it has run for.
CurrentStreak.title: CurrentStreak

FailureMode.description: How a ball that was in play went out.
FailureMode.title: FailureMode

FaultModeShares.description:
How one serve number's faults split between the three ways a serve misses.

Percentages of that serve number's faults, each rounded on its own, so the three
need not come to exactly 100.
FaultModeShares.title: FaultModeShares

FaultModeSplit.description:
A side's fault modes, split by serve number.

A half is null until that serve number has faulted, and both are null on the
returning side throughout: capture records where the tracked player's own serve
missed and nothing at all about the opponent's.
FaultModeSplit.title: FaultModeSplit

LastFiveStats.description:
A player's card figures over their five most recent matches holding points (#260).

Its own window, deliberately not the calendar year the fields beside it use: a
roster card reads as current form, where the leaderboard and the attention
snapshot read as a season. Nor is it `last5_results`'s window, which is the five
most recent matches carrying a result. These are point figures, so a match enters
this one once it holds points, whether or not anyone has recorded who won it, and
is passed over while it holds none. The two fields can cover different matches.
LastFiveStats.title: LastFiveStats

MatchCaptureClaim.description: The device asking to capture a match, named by an id it mints and keeps.
MatchCaptureClaim.title: MatchCaptureClaim

MatchCaptureRead.description: A live capture claim: who holds the match, and when the claim lapses.
MatchCaptureRead.title: MatchCaptureRead

MatchInProgressRead.description: A match with capture under way, as the resume banner shows it.
MatchInProgressRead.title: MatchInProgressRead

MatchResult.description: Whether the tracked player won, from their side and never the opponent's.
MatchResult.title: MatchResult

MatchSetRead.description: One set's game score, as the server derives it from the match's checkpoints and points.
MatchSetRead.title: MatchSetRead

MatchSide.description: One side of a match, the coach's tracked player or their opponent.
MatchSide.title: MatchSide

Metric.description: One number a coach is shown, with everything needed to judge it.
Metric.title: Metric

MetricUnit.description: How a metric's value is scaled, so the client can label and cap it.
MetricUnit.title: MetricUnit

NoteFocus.description: A training focus area a note is filed under.
NoteFocus.title: NoteFocus

OpponentSummary.description: One opponent a player has met, as the scope panel's picker lists them (#244).
OpponentSummary.title: OpponentSummary

OutcomeMixRow.description:
How the points one side decided split between their forcing shots and errors.

Percentages of the rally-ended points that side's own last shot settled. A clean
winner counts as forced: capture records no distinction between the two (#175).
OutcomeMixRow.title: OutcomeMixRow

PlayerCreatedRead.description:
The created player, plus the one password their sign-in starts from.

Shown here and never again: only a hash is stored, so the coach copies the
username and password out of this response and hands them over out of band.
PlayerCreatedRead.title: PlayerCreatedRead

PlayerNoteCreate.description: A coach's note about one player. The player is the path, never the body.
PlayerNoteCreate.title: PlayerNoteCreate

PlayerNoteUpdate.description:
Every field a note may change after it is written, each optional.

player_id is absent for MatchUpdate's reason: a note reaches its owner through its
player, so a writable one would let a note walk across that ownership boundary.
PlayerNoteUpdate.title: PlayerNoteUpdate

PlayerOverview.description: The overview tab: headline metrics and the win/loss record.
PlayerOverview.title: PlayerOverview

PlayerPasswordRead.description: A freshly minted sign-in for one player. The password is shown here only.
PlayerPasswordRead.title: PlayerPasswordRead

PlayerSelfRead.description: A player's own profile, as the player-facing routes answer with it.
PlayerSelfRead.title: PlayerSelfRead

PlayerTransferCodeRead.description: A code handing one player, with their match history, to another coach.
PlayerTransferCodeRead.title: PlayerTransferCodeRead

PointBatch.description:
One flush of a device's capture outbox, for one match.

Ingestion is all-or-nothing: the batch lands whole or nothing in it does, so a
flush is one thing for the sync layer to acknowledge or park. Re-sending a point
already stored is a no-op rather than an error, which is what makes a retried
flush safe.
PointBatch.title: PointBatch

PointCreate.description:
One captured point, exactly as the capture client's scoring engine stamped it.

Validated for shape alone, never for tennis-logic coherence: the client that
scored the match is the only rulebook, so a stamp the server disagrees with is
still stored as sent.
PointCreate.title: PointCreate

PointEnderKind.description: Which of the three ways a rally-ending point ended a style card counts.
PointEnderKind.title: PointEnderKind

PointEnderStyle.description: One point-ender card, with the drill-down behind it.
PointEnderStyle.title: PointEnderStyle

PointEnderStyleDetail.description:
What one style's points looked like, where there is anything to describe.

Wing and shot type are the last successful shot (#175); the zone is where the
final ball landed, a different fact. A point that recorded neither, a missed
return among them, still counts toward the style and appears in no breakdown.
PointEnderStyleDetail.title: PointEnderStyleDetail

PointEnderStyles.description:
Point enders for both halves of the won/lost toggle.

`you` counts the points the player won and `opponents` the ones they lost, each
as three styles in the order forced, unforced, unusual. Aces and double faults
are serve endings and belong to the serve tab, so a side's three counts
deliberately fall short of its points.
PointEnderStyles.title: PointEnderStyles

PointPhase.description: Which stamped moment of a match a points query counts.
PointPhase.title: PointPhase

PointRead.description:
One stored point, as the analytics dashboard and the capture client's sync
reconciliation read it back.

Carries match_id, for symmetry with MatchSetRead's own match-scoped rows, but not
created_at or updated_at: a point is never rewritten after it lands, only deleted,
so those would only restate when the row was ingested, which is bookkeeping neither
reader needs.
PointRead.title: PointRead

RallyBucket.description:
A coarse rally-length bucket, b1 through b4.

The capture screen the coach taps (`rally-length-screen.tsx`) is what defines these
ranges; anywhere else a range is displayed or averaged should match it rather than
settle on its own bounds.
RallyBucket.title: RallyBucket

RallyLengthAverages.description:
Mean rally length in shots, for points won and for points lost (#261).

Approximate by construction: capture stores a coarse bucket rather than a shot count
(#175), so every point counts as its bucket's midpoint, and an ending that never
became a rally carries the shortest bucket here as it does in the histogram.
RallyLengthAverages.title: RallyLengthAverages

RallyLengthBucket.description:
How many points ran to roughly this many shots before ending.

Not scoped to who won them: the read this exists for, serve and return pressure
against fitness, cuts across that.
RallyLengthBucket.title: RallyLengthBucket

RallyStats.description:
The rally tab: how points end once the ball is in play.

The stored shot is the last successful one, so `won_by_shot` describes the
player's own point-winning shots and `lost_by_shot` the opponent's shots the
player lost points on, never the player's own misses (#175).
RallyStats.title: RallyStats

ReturnOutcome.description: The return's outcome, set only on a point the opponent served.
ReturnOutcome.title: ReturnOutcome

ReturnOutcomeSplit.description:
The tracked player's own return outcomes, split by the serve returned.

Percentages of that serve number's recorded returns. Empty on the serving side
throughout: capture records the player's return of the opponent's serve and
nothing about the opponent's return of theirs.
ReturnOutcomeSplit.title: ReturnOutcomeSplit

ScoreCheckpointBatch.description:
One flush of a device's queued checkpoints, for one match, all-or-nothing like
a point batch and idempotent on each checkpoint's id.
ScoreCheckpointBatch.title: ScoreCheckpointBatch

ScoreCheckpointCreate.description:
One checkpoint as the capture client's score editor recorded it.

Shape only, as with a point: the client is the rulebook, so nothing here asks
whether 6-5 can close a set under the match's scoring system.
ScoreCheckpointCreate.title: ScoreCheckpointCreate

ScoreCheckpointRead.description:
One stored checkpoint, read back beside the match's points. No timestamps, for
PointRead's reason: the row is never corrected, only deleted.
ScoreCheckpointRead.title: ScoreCheckpointRead

ScoreSnapshot.description:
The whole scoreboard, set 1 first with no gaps: the last entry is the set in
progress, or the set that decided the match.
ScoreSnapshot.title: ScoreSnapshot

ScoreSnapshotSet.description:
One set of the declared scoreboard: games each, the breaker if one was played,
and who took the set, stamped by the client for the same reason `is_set_end` is:
the server never replays the rules to work it out.
ScoreSnapshotSet.title: ScoreSnapshotSet

ScoringSystem.description: The scoring system the match is played under.
ScoringSystem.title: ScoringSystem

ServeOutcome.description: How a single serve attempt landed.
ServeOutcome.title: ServeOutcome

ServeOutcomeShares.description:
How one serve number's attempts split between the three ways one lands.

Three disjoint percentages totalling 100, so `landed` counts a serve that went in
without being an ace. The share of that serve number that landed in at all, the
figure the card headlines, is `landed + ace`.
ServeOutcomeShares.title: ServeOutcomeShares

ServeOutcomeSplit.description:
A side's serve outcomes, split by serve number.

Whoever served on a side's points owns them, as the trend line does, so the
returning card's describe the opponent's serve. A half is null until that serve
number has been attempted.
ServeOutcomeSplit.title: ServeOutcomeSplit

ServeSideStats.description: One side of the serve tab, serving or returning.
ServeSideStats.title: ServeSideStats

ServeStats.description: The serve tab, both sides in one payload.
ServeStats.title: ServeStats

ServeTrendPoint.description: One match's serve-in rates, as a point on the recent-matches trend line.
ServeTrendPoint.title: ServeTrendPoint

ShotFrequencySides.description:
The radar's shares for both halves of the won/lost toggle.

`you` describes the shots that won the player points and `opponents` the shots
they lost points to, each a share of that side's own total.
ShotFrequencySides.title: ShotFrequencySides

ShotShare.description: One radar axis: a shot type's share of one side's point-ending shots.
ShotShare.title: ShotShare

ShotType.description: The last successful shot of the point.
ShotType.title: ShotType

SquadMemberStats.description:
One roster player's raw figures, for every screen that reads a whole squad.

Inputs and never a verdict: which of these amounts to needing attention (#204),
or to first place on the Squad stats leaderboard (#237), is the client's rule, so
the thresholds live there and the windows live here. Three of them, each named in
the field carrying it since `last5_stats` repeats several of these figures over a
window of its own (#263): the `period_` fields are the calendar year, `last5_results`
is the five most recent results, and `last5_stats` is the roster card's five-match
form window (#260).
SquadMemberStats.title: SquadMemberStats

SquadMetric.description: Which roster-wide figure a squad trend series carries.
SquadMetric.title: SquadMetric

SquadTrendPoint.description: One week of the roster-wide trend line.
SquadTrendPoint.title: SquadTrendPoint

TrackedStat.description:
One statistic's latest value beside the player's own recent baseline.

Both stats here are oriented so a higher `current` is the better direction, which
is what lets the client read a value below the mean as worse than usual for this
player whichever stat it belongs to.
TrackedStat.title: TrackedStat

TrackedStatKey.description: Which statistic one tracked-stat row carries.
TrackedStatKey.title: TrackedStatKey

UnusualReason.description: Why an UNUSUAL point ended, set only alongside that EndReason.
UnusualReason.title: UnusualReason

WinLossRecord.description: Wins and losses, counted over matches with a recorded result.
WinLossRecord.title: WinLossRecord

WingSplit.description: One style's setup shots, counted by the wing they were struck off.
WingSplit.title: WingSplit

post.description:
Replace this coach's password, given the current one, and end every session.

The caller keeps working on a freshly issued session cookie. A wrong current password
answers 403, a missing or dead session 401, and a new password `set_password`'s policy
refuses 400, that one after the 403, so a wrong current password is what a caller
getting both wrong hears about first.

502.description: Couldn't send that code, please try again

post.description:
Replace this player's password, given the current one, and end every session.

The caller keeps working on a freshly issued session cookie. A wrong current
password answers 403, a missing or dead session 401, and a new password the
policy refuses 400, that one after the 403, so a caller getting both wrong hears
about the current password first.

502.description: Couldn't send that code, please try again

post.description:
Set the new password, given the cookie verify-reset-code minted.

A 401 means that cookie is missing, spent, expired, or was earned for a different
address, so the coach has to answer a code again. A 400 means the code was fine but
`set_password`'s policy refused the new password. Every live session ends here.

delete.description:
Sign out every other client holding a session for this coach.

The calling device stays signed in, on a session issued here rather than the one it
arrived with. A coach revoking after a borrowed laptop or a lost phone does so from
the device in their hand, and dropping that one mid-action would be the wrong
surprise.

post.description:
Answer a reset code without spending it, for the cookie reset-password demands.

A code that is wrong, expired, already answered, or asked for an address holding no
account all answer the same 400, so nothing here says whether an account exists.

delete.description:
Erase this coach and everything recorded under them, given their password.

Refused with a 409 while any player is still on the roster, so that someone another
coach is about to take over is not erased by an account closing: clear each one
first, by transfer or by deletion. `delete_players` waives that refusal and takes
the whole roster along, for the coach who means to leave nothing behind, but not a
live transfer code on any player, which refuses closure either way.

409.description: Players must be transferred or deleted first, or Outstanding transfer codes must be cancelled or redeemed first

delete.description: Clear this coach's profile photo, back to the app's initials avatar.

post.description: Replace this coach's profile photo, and answer with the coach.

400.description: That file is not an image, Photos must be JPEG, PNG or WebP, or That image has too many pixels — resize it before uploading

post.description: Answer whether this is the signed-in coach's password, changing nothing.

get.description:
Every match of this coach's that capture is under way on, freshest claim first.

The web client's own resume banner is device-local by design, not a caller here: the
points behind a match live in the capturing device's IndexedDB, so a Resume button on
a second device could not replay them even knowing the match exists. What this route
answers instead is what the server itself can see of capture in flight, and the claim
behind it is what guards a delete from a second device (`capture_holder`, below) — a
coach-scoped read, though the claim itself names a device, for whichever caller does
want the cross-device picture this device-local banner deliberately isn't.

delete.description:
Erase one match and the points captured against it, unless another device holds it.

`device_id` names the asking device, so the device holding the capture claim can
still delete the match it is capturing. A player's analytics change retroactively and
that is the intent: a match started against the wrong player skews every statistic it
is counted in until it goes.

409.description: A completed match's result or scoring system cannot be changed

get.description:
A match's points, in the order the capture client assigned them.

Feeds two readers: the analytics dashboard aggregating over rally outcomes and
serve placement, and the capture client reconciling its local outbox against what
the server holds after a sync. A pure read, so match_for_coach takes no lock.

post.description:
Ingest one flush of captured points, answering with the match's set scores.

All or nothing: the batch lands whole or none of it does, and a point already
stored is left as it is rather than rewritten, so a retried or overlapping flush
converges instead of failing. `points` carries the batch's own ceiling, and the
1 MB request body limit is the real bound, which a batch of points carrying long
notes reaches sooner.

delete.description: Erase one point the coach undid, and rederive the set scores without it.

get.description: A match's score checkpoints, in sequence order, read back beside its points.

post.description:
Ingest one flush of score checkpoints, answering with the match's set scores.

The point ingest's contract, row for row: all or nothing, a checkpoint already
stored is left as it is, a completed match refuses, and the flush renews this
device's capture claim. The set scores come back recomputed with the newest
checkpoint folded in.

delete.description: Erase one checkpoint the coach undid, and rederive the set scores without it.

post.description:
Take the player a transfer code names onto this coach's roster, matches included.

The code is spent here, so presenting it again answers 400. The match history needs no
rewriting: a match reaches its owner through its player, so it moves with them.

400.description: That transfer code is unknown or has already been used

409.description: That player is already on your roster

delete.description:
Erase this player and every match recorded against them. Nothing undoes it.

No confirmation beyond the request itself. What the coach is about to lose is on the
screen in front of them, so confirming it belongs to the client rather than to a
second round trip taken courtside.

409.description: Outstanding transfer codes must be cancelled or redeemed first

because it is the one spelling of a matchup that cannot vary. `surface`, if given,
narrows the count to that surface (#225), so the picker's own numbers describe
the scope a coach is about to apply rather than the whole career; an opponent with
no matches on that surface is dropped rather than shown at zero, since it is not a
real option to pick.

delete.description: Erase one note. Nothing undoes it, and nothing else goes with it.

post.description:
Mint a fresh one-time password for this player, ending their live sessions.

This is also how a player who existed before sign-ins, or who forgot their
password, gets one: players have no email, so their coach is the recovery path.

delete.description: Clear this player's photo, back to the initials avatar the app falls back to.

post.description: Replace this player's photo, and answer with the player.

400.description: That file is not an image, Photos must be JPEG, PNG or WebP, or That image has too many pixels — resize it before uploading

delete.description:
Cancel an outstanding code, so a copy of it stops working.

A code that never expires needs a way back, since handing one to the wrong person is
otherwise permanent. 204 whether or not one was outstanding, as logout is: the request
asks for a state, and a player with no live code is already in it.

post.description:
Mint a code that hands this player, their notes and their matches, to another coach.

Asking again replaces the previous code, which the storage decides rather than the
policy: only a hash is kept, so an earlier code can never be shown a second time.

get.description:
Per-player squad figures, one row per roster player.

Serves every screen that reads a whole roster: the home screen's snapshot (#204),
the Squad stats leaderboard and headline (#237), and the Players tab's per-player
card (#260), so one request paints a list of any length. The thresholds that turn
these numbers into a flag or a rank are the web app's (`lib/analytics/attention.ts`,
`lib/analytics/squad-stats.ts`); what this endpoint owns is the windows they are
measured over. The period is the calendar year, as the overview tab's season
record is, and scopes `matches_logged_this_period` and every field the `period_`
prefix names; the streak, the last five results and the days since the
last match are counted over every match, so a run that started in December is
still a run in January. A tracked stat's `current` is its value over the latest
match that can answer it, against a baseline of the ten matches before that one.

Both period rates pool the period's points rather than averaging its matches, so
a four-point match weighs what four points are worth.

`last5_stats` has a window of its own: the player's five most recent matches that
hold points, resulted or not, which is what a roster card means by current form.
That is not `last5_results`'s five, which are the five most recent matches
carrying a result, so the two fields can cover different matches. It carries its own
copies of the period's point figures rather than re-scoping them, because the two
screens above read those as a season (#260).

`surface`, if given, narrows every count above to matches on that surface (#225).
A player with none on the requested surface still returns a zeroed row rather
than dropping off the roster — the same rule the empty-roster row above follows.

parameters.description: Count only matches played on this surface (#225).
parameters.name: surface

schema.description: Count only matches played on this surface (#225).
schema.title: Surface

get.description:
One roster-wide figure a week, over the six weeks ending with the last match.

Weeks run Monday to Sunday, so a weekend's fixtures land in one bucket rather
than split across two, and the sixth is the week the roster last played in rather
than the week today falls in (#278). All six come back in order, so a quiet
fortnight inside the window draws a gap in the line rather than a shorter line.

A week's figure pools every match the roster played in it rather than averaging
the roster's players, for the reason the period's own rates are pooled: one match
is one match's worth of evidence whoever played it, where a per-player mean would
weigh a player's single match against another's four. A week whose matches cannot
answer the metric, one with no recorded result, no unforced error or no serve
among them, carries a null rather than a zero.

`surface`, if given, narrows every week's pooled matches to that surface (#225).
